items.title: Louis Nelson Interview, 1960-04-18
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] I remember Baby Dobbs, the drummer, told me about. [INTERVIEWEE] Yeah, very certainly.

ctx.x: And the captain on that boat, he's a very peculiar fella. He wants you to... He set the 10-4 for you. He'd get out there with his watch. He'd time you. He wanted... It's got to be just right. And you got 12 numbers to play a night, and you got to get them all in. That was one of the... That's Captain Roy's Streckfus. Roy's Streckfus. He had to take orders from his brother, Joe Streckfus. That's the man one. He stays in St. Louis. He don't come down there.
I remember Baby Dobbs, the drummer, told me about.

Yeah, very certainly. When that boat be coming, he be standing on that barge waiting. You see how it's going to land. And then he walk on, he send orders down there, and he'd look around, see if everything fixed just the way he ordered it. Well, it's a nice trip. It's the hardest part is going upstream, you see. You go so slow. Yeah. Then you make those stops. Coming down is all right. See, you're coming with the current.
